translations.idiomatic: He abandoned the guard of crossed halberds and cast aside the rites befitting Heaven's chosen, hurried through market gates, sang drunkenly in taverns, roamed at night and forgot to return, feasted and slept in barracks, seized men's wives and daughters, and plundered their goods—things unrecorded in the law codes, unheard of since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 沈勃儒士，孫超功臣，幼文兄弟，並豫勳効，四人無罪，一朝同戮。

translations.literal: Shen Bo was a Confucian scholar; Sun Chaozhi a meritorious minister; the brothers Youwen—all had shared in the dynasty's achievements. The four were guiltless, yet in a single morning were slain together.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Bo was a Confucian scholar, Sun Chaozhi a meritorious minister, and the brothers Youwen had all shared in the dynasty's achievements. The four were guiltless, yet in a single morning were slain together.

sentences.zh: 飛鏃鼓劍，孩稚無遺，屠裂肝腸，以為戲謔，投骸江流，以為歡笑。

translations.literal: With flying arrows and clashing swords, not even infants were spared; he tore open livers and bowels for sport and cast corpses into the river for laughter.
translations.idiomatic: With flying arrows and clashing swords not even infants were spared; he tore open livers and bowels for sport and cast corpses into the river for laughter.

sentences.zh: 又淫費無度，帑藏空竭，橫賦關河，專充別蓄，黔庶嗷嗷，厝生無所。

translations.literal: Again he squandered without limit until the treasury was emptied; he levied taxes across the passes and rivers to fill private hoards, while the common people wailed and had nowhere to set down their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Again he squandered without limit until the treasury was emptied; he levied taxes across the passes and rivers to fill private hoards, while the common people wailed and had nowhere to live.

sentences.zh: 吾與其所生每厲以義方，遂謀酖毒，將騁凶忿。

translations.literal: I and his birth-mother repeatedly exhorted him with righteous teaching, whereupon he plotted poison to unleash his savage rage.
translations.idiomatic: I and his birth-mother repeatedly exhorted him with righteous teaching, whereupon he plotted poison to unleash his savage rage.

sentences.zh: 沈憂假日，慮不終朝。

translations.literal: Deep anxiety consumed my days; I feared I would not survive till morning.
translations.idiomatic: Deep anxiety consumed my days; I feared I would not survive till morning.

sentences.zh: 自昔辛、癸，爰及幽、厲，方之於此，未譬萬分。

translations.literal: From ancient Xin and Gui down to You and Li—compared with this, they do not reach one ten-thousandth.
translations.idiomatic: From the ancient tyrants Xin and Gui down to You and Li of Zhou—compared with this, they do not reach one ten-thousandth.

sentences.zh: 民怨既深，神怒已積，七廟阽危，四海褫氣。

translations.literal: The people's resentment had grown deep, Heaven's wrath had long accumulated; the seven ancestral temples stood on the brink of ruin, and the four seas lost their breath.
translations.idiomatic: The people's resentment had grown deep and Heaven's wrath long accumulated; the seven ancestral temples stood on the brink of ruin, and the four seas lost their breath.

sentences.zh: 廢昏立明，前代令範，況迺滅義反道，天人所棄，釁深牧野，理絕桐宮。

translations.literal: Deposing the benighted and enthroning the enlightened is a fine model of former ages; how much more when one extinguishes righteousness and turns against the Way, abandoned by Heaven and men alike—guilt deep as at Muye, reason severed as at Tong Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Deposing the benighted and enthroning the enlightened is a fine model of former ages; how much more when one extinguishes righteousness and turns against the Way, abandoned by Heaven and men alike—guilt as deep as at Muye, reason severed as at Tong Palace.

sentences.zh: 故密令蕭領軍潛運明略，幽顯協規，普天同泰。

translations.literal: Therefore I secretly ordered General Xiao to move with enlightened strategy; the hidden and the manifest joined in one design, and universal peace was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I secretly ordered General Xiao to move with enlightened strategy; the hidden and the manifest joined in one design, and universal peace was restored.

sentences.zh: 驃騎大將軍安成王體自太宗，天挺淹叡，風神凝遠，德映在田。

translations.literal: General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry Prince of Ancheng is descended from Taizong; Heaven endowed him with deep wisdom, his bearing is composed and far-reaching, and his virtue shines even in humble retirement.
translations.idiomatic: General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry Prince of Ancheng is descended from Taizong; Heaven endowed him with deep wisdom, his bearing is composed and far-reaching, and his virtue shines even in humble retirement.

sentences.zh: 地隆親茂，皇曆攸歸，億兆係心，含生屬望。

translations.literal: His rank in the clan is lofty and his kinship flourishing; the imperial chronology returns to him, the hundred millions bind their hearts to him, and all living beings look to him.
translations.idiomatic: His rank in the clan is lofty and his kinship flourishing; the imperial chronology returns to him, the hundred millions bind their hearts to him, and all living beings look to him.

sentences.zh: 宜光奉祖宗，臨享萬國。

translations.literal: It is fitting that he brightly serve the ancestors and preside over the myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting that he brightly serve the ancestors and preside over the myriad states.

sentences.zh: 便依舊典，以時奉行。

translations.literal: Let the old rites be followed and enacted in due season.
translations.idiomatic: Let the old rites be followed and enacted in due season.

sentences.zh: 未亡人追往傷懷，永言感絕。

translations.literal: I, the survivor, look back in grief; my words end in boundless sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: I, the survivor, look back in grief; my words end in boundless sorrow.

sentences.zh: 太后又令曰：「昱窮凶極暴，自取灰滅，雖曰罪招，能無傷悼。

translations.literal: The empress dowager issued another edict: "Yu was utterly vicious and savage and brought ruin upon himself; though his crimes invited this end, how can one not mourn?
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager issued another edict: "Yu was utterly vicious and savage and brought ruin upon himself; though his crimes invited this end, how can one not mourn?

sentences.zh: 棄同品庶，顧所不忍。

translations.literal: To cast him out like the common multitude is more than the heart can bear.
translations.idiomatic: To cast him out like the common multitude is more than the heart can bear.

sentences.zh: 可特追封蒼梧郡王。

translations.literal: Let him be specially posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Cangwu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be specially posthumously enfeoffed as prince of Cangwu commandery.

sentences.zh: 」葬丹陽秣陵縣郊壇西。

translations.literal: " He was buried west of the suburban altar in Moling county, Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: " He was buried west of the suburban altar in Moling county, Danyang.

sentences.zh: 初昱在東宮，年五六歲時，始就書學，而惰業好嬉戲，主帥不能禁。

translations.literal: When Yu was in the Eastern Palace, at five or six years of age he first began book learning, yet he was idle in his studies and fond of play; his tutors could not restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu was in the Eastern Palace, at five or six he first began book learning, yet he was idle in his studies and fond of play; his tutors could not restrain him.

sentences.zh: 好緣漆帳竿，去地丈餘，如此者半食久，乃下。

translations.literal: He loved to climb the lacquered curtain poles, more than ten feet above the ground; he would stay there for half a meal before coming down.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to climb the lacquered curtain poles more than ten feet above the ground and would stay there for half a meal before coming down.

sentences.zh: 年漸長，喜怒乖節，左右有失旨者，輒手加撲打。

translations.literal: As he grew older his joy and anger lost all measure; whenever those around him failed his wish he would beat them with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older his joy and anger lost all measure; whenever those around him displeased him he would beat them with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 徒跣蹲踞，以此為常。

translations.literal: Barefoot and squatting—this became his habit.
translations.idiomatic: Barefoot and squatting—this became his habit.

sentences.zh: 主帥以白太宗，上輒敕昱所生，嚴加捶訓。

translations.literal: The tutors reported this to Taizong, and the emperor would order Yu's birth-mother to beat and instruct him severely.
translations.idiomatic: The tutors reported this to Taizong, and the emperor would order Yu's birth-mother to beat and instruct him severely.

sentences.zh: 及嗣位，內畏太后，外憚諸大臣，猶未得肆志。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the throne he feared the empress dowager within and the chief ministers without, and still could not fully indulge his will.
translations.idiomatic: When he succeeded to the throne he feared the empress dowager within and the chief ministers without, and still could not fully indulge his will.

sentences.zh: 自加元服，變態轉興，內外稍無以制。

translations.literal: After he received the cap-and-gown of adulthood his transformation grew ever sharper, and gradually none within or without could restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: After he received the cap-and-gown of adulthood his transformation grew ever sharper, and gradually none within or without could restrain him.

sentences.zh: 三年秋冬間，便好出遊行，太妃每乘青篾車，隨相檢攝。

translations.literal: Between autumn and winter in the third year he took to going out on excursions; the imperial consort mother would ride in a green bamboo carriage and follow to keep watch.
translations.idiomatic: Between autumn and winter in the third year he took to going out on excursions; the imperial consort mother would ride in a green bamboo carriage and follow to keep watch.

sentences.zh: 昱漸自放恣，太妃不復能禁。

translations.literal: Yu gradually gave himself over to license, and the imperial consort mother could no longer restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu gradually gave himself over to license, and the imperial consort mother could no longer restrain him.

sentences.zh: 單將左右，棄部伍，或十里、二十里，或入市里，或往營署，日暮乃歸。

translations.literal: Alone with a few attendants he abandoned his escort, sometimes for ten or twenty li, sometimes entering market wards, sometimes going to barracks, and returned only at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Alone with a few attendants he abandoned his escort, sometimes for ten or twenty li, sometimes entering market wards, sometimes going to barracks, and returned only at dusk.

sentences.zh: 四年春夏，此行彌數。

translations.literal: In spring and summer of the fourth year such outings became ever more frequent.
translations.idiomatic: In spring and summer of the fourth year such outings became ever more frequent.

sentences.zh: 自京城剋定，意志轉驕，於是無日不出。

translations.literal: Once the capital had been secured his will turned ever prouder, and from then on not a day passed without his going out.
translations.idiomatic: Once the capital had been secured his will turned ever prouder, and from then on not a day passed without his going out.

sentences.zh: 與左右人解僧智、張五兒恒相馳逐，夜出，開承明門，夕去晨反，晨出暮歸。

translations.literal: With his attendants Jie Sengzhi and Zhang Wu'er he constantly raced in pursuit; at night they opened Chenming Gate, leaving at dusk and returning at dawn, or leaving at dawn and returning at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: With his attendants Jie Sengzhi and Zhang Wu'er he constantly raced in pursuit; at night they opened Chenming Gate, leaving at dusk and returning at dawn, or leaving at dawn and returning at dusk.

sentences.zh: 從者並執鋋矛，行人男女，及犬馬牛驢，值無免者。

translations.literal: Those who followed all carried halberds and spears; men and women among travelers, and dogs, horses, oxen, and donkeys—none who met them escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Those who followed all carried halberds and spears; men and women among travelers, and dogs, horses, oxen, and donkeys—none who met them escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 民間擾懼，晝日不敢開門，道上行人殆絕。

translations.literal: The people were alarmed and afraid; by day they dared not open their doors, and travelers on the roads nearly vanished.
translations.idiomatic: The people were alarmed and afraid; by day they dared not open their doors, and travelers on the roads nearly vanished.

sentences.zh: 常著小袴褶，未嘗服衣冠。

translations.literal: He constantly wore short trousers and jackets and never put on cap and gown.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly wore short trousers and jackets and never put on cap and gown.

sentences.zh: 或有忤意，輒加以虐刑。

translations.literal: Whenever anyone displeased him he would inflict cruel punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever anyone displeased him he would inflict cruel punishment.

sentences.zh: 有白棓數十枚，各有名號，鍼椎鑿鋸之徒，不離左右。

translations.literal: He kept several dozen white clubs, each with its own name; needles, awls, chisels, and saws never left his side.
translations.idiomatic: He kept several dozen white clubs, each with its own name; needles, awls, chisels, and saws never left his side.

sentences.zh: 嘗以鐵椎椎人陰破，左右人見之有斂眉者，昱大怒，令此人袒胛正立，以矛刺胛洞過。

translations.literal: Once he smashed a man's groin with an iron awl; when an attendant who saw it frowned, Yu flew into a rage, ordered the man to bare his back and stand upright, and drove a spear through his shoulder blade.
translations.idiomatic: Once he smashed a man's groin with an iron awl; when an attendant who saw it frowned, Yu flew into a rage, ordered the man to bare his back and stand upright, and drove a spear through his shoulder blade.

sentences.zh: 於耀靈殿上養驢數十頭，所自乘馬，養於御牀側。

translations.literal: On the terrace of Yaoling Hall he kept several dozen donkeys; the horse he himself rode was kept beside the imperial couch.
translations.idiomatic: On the terrace of Yaoling Hall he kept several dozen donkeys; the horse he himself rode was kept beside the imperial couch.

sentences.zh: 先是民間訛言，謂太宗不男，陳太妃本李道兒妾，道路之言，或云道兒子也。

translations.literal: Earlier a false rumor among the people said Taizong was not a man; the Chen imperial consort mother had originally been a concubine of Li Dao'er, and street talk sometimes said Yu was Dao'er's son.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a false rumor among the people said Taizong was not a man; the Chen imperial consort mother had originally been a concubine of Li Dao'er, and street talk sometimes said Yu was Dao'er's son.

sentences.zh: 昱每出入去來，常自稱劉統，或自號李將軍。

translations.literal: Whenever Yu went out or came in he often called himself Liu Tong, or styled himself General Li.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yu went out or came in he often called himself Liu Tong, or styled himself General Li.

sentences.zh: 與右衞翼輦營女子私通，每從之遊，持數千錢，供酒肉之費。

translations.literal: He had secret relations with a woman of the Right Guard Wing-Litter Guard and went out with her whenever she traveled, carrying several thousand coins to pay for wine and meat.
translations.idiomatic: He had secret relations with a woman of the Right Guard Wing-Litter Guard and went out with her whenever she traveled, carrying several thousand coins to pay for wine and meat.

sentences.zh: 阮佃夫腹心人張羊為佃夫所委信。

translations.literal: Zhang Yang, a trusted man of Ruan Tianfu, was one in whom Tianfu placed full confidence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yang, a trusted man of Ruan Tianfu, was one in whom Tianfu placed full confidence.

sentences.zh: 佃夫敗，叛走，後捕得，昱自於承明門以車轢殺之。

translations.literal: When Tianfu fell, Yang fled in rebellion; later he was captured, and Yu personally had him crushed to death with a cart at Chenming Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianfu fell, Yang fled in rebellion; later he was captured, and Yu personally had him crushed to death with a cart at Chenming Gate.

sentences.zh: 杜延載、沈勃、杜幼文、孫超，皆躬運矛鋋，手自臠割。

translations.literal: Du Yanzai, Shen Bo, Du Youwen, and Sun Chao—all personally wielded spear and halberd and dismembered men with their own hands.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yanzai, Shen Bo, Du Youwen, and Sun Chao—all personally wielded spear and halberd and dismembered men with their own hands.

sentences.zh: 執幼文兄叔文於玄武湖北，昱馳馬執矟，自往刺之。

translations.literal: When Youwen's elder brother Shuwen was seized north of Xuanwu Lake, Yu galloped there with a spear in hand and personally ran him through.
translations.idiomatic: When Youwen's elder brother Shuwen was seized north of Xuanwu Lake, Yu galloped there with a spear in hand and personally ran him through.

sentences.zh: 制露車一乘，其上施篷，乘以出入，從者不過數十人。

translations.literal: He had a single open carriage made with an awning erected upon it and used it when going out; those who followed numbered no more than several dozen.
translations.idiomatic: He had a single open carriage made with an awning erected upon it and used it when going out; those who followed numbered no more than several dozen.

sentences.zh: 羽儀追之恒不及；

translations.literal: The imperial guard in pursuit could never catch up;
translations.idiomatic: The imperial guard in pursuit could never catch up;

sentences.zh: 又各慮禍，亦不敢追尋，唯整部伍，別在一處瞻望而已。

translations.literal: each also feared disaster and dared not pursue, but only kept ranks whole and watched from another place.
translations.idiomatic: each also feared disaster and dared not pursue, but only kept ranks whole and watched from another place.

sentences.zh: 凡諸鄙事，過目則能，鍛鍊金銀，裁衣作帽，莫不精絕。

translations.literal: Of all vulgar crafts, whatever he saw he could do; forging and refining gold and silver, cutting clothes and making caps—nothing was not exquisitely done.
translations.idiomatic: Of all vulgar crafts, whatever he saw he could do; forging and refining gold and silver, cutting clothes and making caps—nothing was not exquisitely done.

sentences.zh: 未嘗吹篪，執管便韻。

translations.literal: He had never blown the chi, yet when he took up the pipe the tones came in tune.
translations.idiomatic: He had never blown the chi, yet when he took up the pipe the tones came in tune.

sentences.zh: 天性好殺，以此為歡，一日無事，輒慘慘不樂。

translations.literal: By nature he loved killing; this was his delight, and on a day when nothing happened he grew gloomy and unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved killing; this was his delight, and on a day when nothing happened he grew gloomy and unhappy.

sentences.zh: 內外百司，人不自保，殿省憂遑，夕不及旦。

translations.literal: Throughout the hundred offices within and without, no man could be sure of himself; the palace departments were anxious and alarmed, and evening did not reach morning before new fear arose.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the hundred offices within and without, no man could be sure of himself; the palace departments were anxious and alarmed, and evening did not reach morning before new fear arose.

sentences.zh: 齊王順天人之心，潛圖廢立，與直閤將軍王敬則謀之。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi, following the people's hearts, secretly plotted deposition and enthronement and consulted with General of the Direct Retinue Wang Jingze.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi, following the people's hearts, secretly plotted deposition and enthronement and consulted with General of the Direct Retinue Wang Jingze.

sentences.zh: 七月七日，昱乘露車，從二百許人，無復鹵簿羽儀，往青園尼寺，晚至新安寺就曇度道人飲酒。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the seventh month Yu rode in his open carriage with about two hundred men, no longer with imperial guards or ceremonial escort, and went to Qingyuan Nunnery; in the evening he reached Xinan Temple and drank with the Daoist priest Tandu.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the seventh month Yu rode in his open carriage with about two hundred men, no longer with imperial guards or ceremonial escort, and went to Qingyuan Nunnery; in the evening he reached Xinan Temple and drank with the Daoist priest Tandu.

sentences.zh: 醉，夕扶還於仁壽殿東阿氈幄中臥。

translations.literal: Drunk, he was helped back in the evening to lie in the felt tent east of Renshou Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, he was helped back in the evening to lie in the felt tent east of Renshou Hall.

sentences.zh: 時昱出入無恒，省內諸閤，夜皆不閉。

translations.literal: At that time Yu came and went without fixed pattern; the various gates within the palace were left unclosed at night.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yu came and went without fixed pattern; the various gates within the palace were left unclosed at night.

sentences.zh: 且羣下畏相逢值，無敢出者。

translations.literal: Moreover the officials below feared meeting him by chance, and none dared go out.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the officials below feared meeting him by chance, and none dared go out.

sentences.zh: 宿衞並逃避，內外無相禁攝。

translations.literal: The night guards all fled; within and without there was no one to restrain or supervise.
translations.idiomatic: The night guards all fled; within and without there was no one to restrain or supervise.

sentences.zh: 王敬則先結昱左右楊玉夫、楊萬年、呂欣之、湯成之、陳奉伯、張石留、羅僧智、鍾千載、嚴道福、雷道賜、戴昭祖、許啟、戚元寶、盛道泰、鍾千秋、王天寶、公上延孫、俞成、錢道寶、馬敬之、陳寶直、吳璩之、劉印魯、唐天寶、俞孫等二十五人，謀共取昱。

translations.literal: Wang Jingze had first won over twenty-five of Yu's attendants—Yang Yufu, Yang Wannian, Lü Xinzhi, Tang Chengzhi, Chen Fengbo, Zhang Shiliu, Luo Sengzhi, Zhong Qianzai, Yan Daofu, Lei Daoci, Dai Zhaozu, Xu Qi, Qi Yuanbao, Sheng Daotai, Zhong Qianqiu, Wang Tianbao, Gongshang Yansun, Yu Cheng, Qian Daobao, Ma Jingzhi, Chen Baozhi, Wu Quzhi, Liu Yinlu, Tang Tianbao, Yu Sun, and others—to plot together to seize Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingze had first won over twenty-five of Yu's attendants—Yang Yufu, Yang Wannian, Lü Xinzhi, Tang Chengzhi, Chen Fengbo, Zhang Shiliu, Luo Sengzhi, Zhong Qianzai, Yan Daofu, Lei Daoci, Dai Zhaozu, Xu Qi, Qi Yuanbao, Sheng Daotai, Zhong Qianqiu, Wang Tianbao, Gongshang Yansun, Yu Cheng, Qian Daobao, Ma Jingzhi, Chen Baozhi, Wu Quzhi, Liu Yinlu, Tang Tianbao, Yu Sun, and others—to plot together to seize Yu.

sentences.zh: 其夕，敬則出外，玉夫見昱醉熟無所知，乃與萬年同入氈幄內，以昱防身刀斬之。

translations.literal: That evening Jingze went outside; Yufu saw that Yu was drunk and unconscious, and together with Wannian entered the felt tent and cut him down with Yu's own side-arm.
translations.idiomatic: That evening Jingze went outside; Yufu saw that Yu was drunk and unconscious, and together with Wannian entered the felt tent and cut him down with Yu's own side-arm.

sentences.zh: 奉伯提昱首，依常行法，稱敕開承明門出，以首與敬則，馳至領軍府，以首呈齊王。

translations.literal: Fengbo lifted Yu's head; according to the usual procedure he declared an edict and opened Chenming Gate to go out, gave the head to Jingze, and galloped to the General-in-Chief's headquarters to present the head to Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Fengbo lifted Yu's head; according to the usual procedure he declared an edict and opened Chenming Gate to go out, gave the head to Jingze, and galloped to the general-in-chief's headquarters to present the head to Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 王乃戎服，率左右數十人，稱行還，開承明門入。

translations.literal: The prince then put on military dress, led several dozen attendants, declared that he was returning from an outing, and entered through Chenming Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The prince then put on military dress, led several dozen attendants, declared that he was returning from an outing, and entered through Chenming Gate.

sentences.zh: 昱他夕每開門，門者震懾不敢視，至是弗之疑。

translations.literal: On other nights whenever Yu opened the gate the gatekeepers were terrified and dared not look up; this time they suspected nothing.
translations.idiomatic: On other nights whenever Yu opened the gate the gatekeepers were terrified and dared not look up; this time they suspected nothing.

sentences.zh: 齊王既入，曉，乃奉太后令奉迎安成王。

translations.literal: Once Prince of Qi had entered, at dawn he then received the empress dowager's order to welcome Prince of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Once Prince of Qi had entered, at dawn he then received the empress dowager's order to welcome Prince of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：喪國亡家之主，雖適末同途，發軫或異也。

translations.literal: The historian says: Lords who lose their states and ruin their houses, though they meet the same end, may set out from different beginnings.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Lords who lose their states and ruin their houses, though they meet the same end, may set out from different beginnings.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝卑遊褻幸，皆龍駕帝飾，傳警清路；

translations.literal: The Former Deposed Emperor debased himself in wandering and intimate favor—all with the dragon carriage and imperial regalia, with guards clearing the road.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Deposed Emperor debased himself in wandering and intimate favor—all with the dragon carriage and imperial regalia, with guards clearing the road.

sentences.zh: 蒼梧王則藏璽懷紱，魚服忘反，危冠短服，匹馬孤征。

translations.literal: Prince of Cangwu hid the seal and wore the cord, forgot he was a fish in imperial dress, wore a perilous crown and short garments, and rode alone on a single horse.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Cangwu hid the seal and wore the cord, forgot he was a fish in imperial dress, wore a perilous crown and short garments, and rode alone on a single horse.

sentences.zh: 至於殞身覆祚，其理若一。

translations.literal: When it came to perishing and overturning the succession, the principle was one.
translations.idiomatic: When it came to perishing and overturning the succession, the principle was one.

sentences.zh: 姬、夏之隆，質文異尚，亡國之道，其亦然乎。

translations.literal: In the flourishing ages of Zhou and Xia, substance and ornament were differently prized—yet the way to lose a state, is it not likewise?
translations.idiomatic: In the flourishing ages of Zhou and Xia, substance and ornament were differently prized—yet the way to lose a state, is it not likewise?

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual collation notes

sentences.zh: 冬十月辛卯 下有辛未。

translations.literal: Below "On xinmao day in the tenth month of winter" there follows xinwei.
translations.idiomatic: Below "On xinmao day in the tenth month of winter" there follows xinwei.

sentences.zh: 按是月庚戌朔，二十二日辛未，無辛卯。

translations.literal: According to this month gengxu was the first day of the month; the twenty-second day was xinwei—there was no xinmao.
translations.idiomatic: That month began on gengxu; the twenty-second day was xinwei—there was no xinmao.

sentences.zh: 以越州刺史陳伯紹為交州刺史 張森楷校勘記云：「按明帝紀，泰始五年，伯紹為交州刺史。

translations.literal: "Inspector of Yuezhou Chen Bozhao was made Inspector of Jiaozhou"—Zhang Senkai's collation notes say: "According to the Annals of Emperor Ming, in the fifth year of Taishi, Bozhao was Inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: "Inspector of Yuezhou Chen Bozhao was made inspector of Jiaozhou": Zhang Senkai's collation notes say: "According to the Annals of Emperor Ming, in the fifth year of Taishi Bozhao was inspector of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 七年，置越州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Yuezhou was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Yuezhou was established.

sentences.zh: 南齊書州郡志云，元徽二年，陳伯紹為越州刺史，當即指此。

translations.literal: The Monograph on Provinces and Commanderies in the History of the Southern Qi says that in the second year of Yuanhui, Chen Bozhao was Inspector of Yuezhou—this must refer to the present passage.
translations.idiomatic: The Monograph on Provinces and Commanderies in the History of the Southern Qi says that in the second year of Yuanhui Chen Bozhao was inspector of Yuezhou—this must refer to the present passage.

sentences.zh: 此當是以交州刺史陳伯紹為越州刺史，刻譌互倒。」

translations.literal: Here it should read that Inspector of Jiaozhou Chen Bozhao was made Inspector of Yuezhou; the carved text has transposed the two."
translations.idiomatic: Here it should read that inspector of Jiaozhou Chen Bozhao was made inspector of Yuezhou; the carved text has transposed the two."

sentences.zh: 五月壬午「壬午」各本並作「壬子」，據南史、建康實錄、通鑑改。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, renwu—"renwu" in all editions is written as "renzi"; it is changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties, the Jiankang Veritable Records, and the Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, renwu: "renwu" in all editions is written as renzi, changed according to the History of the Southern Dynasties, the Jiankang Veritable Records, and Zizhi Tongjian.

sentences.zh: 按是月辛未朔，十三日壬午，無壬子。

translations.literal: According to this month xinwei was the first day of the month; the thirteenth day was renwu—there was no renzi.
translations.idiomatic: That month began on xinwei; the thirteenth day was renwu—there was no renzi.

sentences.zh: 賊黨杜黑蠡丁文豪分軍向朱雀航「杜黑蠡」魏書作「杜黑騾」。

translations.literal: The rebel band under Du Heili and Ding Wenhao divided their forces toward the Zhuque Bridge—"Du Heili" in the History of the Northern Wei is written as "Du Heiluo."
translations.idiomatic: The rebel band under Du Heili and Ding Wenhao divided their forces toward the Zhuque Bridge: "Du Heili" in the History of the Northern Wei is written as Du Heiluo.

sentences.zh: 甲午 各本並作「戊午」，據局本及南史、建康實錄改。

translations.literal: jiawu—in all editions it is written as wuwu; it is changed according to the Bureau edition and the History of the Southern Dynasties and the Jiankang Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: Jiawu: all editions read wuwu, corrected per the Bureau edition, the History of the Southern Dynasties, and the Jiankang Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 是月辛未朔，二十四日甲午，無戊午。

translations.literal: This month xinwei was the first day of the month; the twenty-fourth day was jiawu—there was no wuwu.
translations.idiomatic: That month began on xinwei; the twenty-fourth day was jiawu—there was no wuwu.

sentences.zh: 撫軍典籤茅恬開東府納賊「撫軍」南史作「車騎」，建康實錄作「護軍」。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk of the Army Who Pacifies the Army Mao Tian opened the Eastern Headquarters to admit the rebels—"Pacifies the Army" in the History of the Southern Dynasties is written as "Chariots and Cavalry," and in the Jiankang Veritable Records as "Protects the Army."
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk of the army who pacifies the army Mao Tian opened the Eastern Headquarters to admit the rebels: "Pacifies the Army" in the History of the Southern Dynasties is written as Chariots and Cavalry, and in the Jiankang Veritable Records as Protects the Army.

sentences.zh: 鎮北將軍南徐州刺史建平王景素進號征北將軍 各本並脫「南」字，據景素傳補。

translations.literal: General Who Stabilizes the North and Inspector of South Xuzhou Prince of Jianping Jingsu was advanced to General Who Campaigns North—in all editions the character "south" is omitted; it is supplied according to Jingsu's biography.
translations.idiomatic: General who stabilizes the north and inspector of South Xuzhou Prince of Jianping Jingsu was advanced to general who campaigns north: all editions omit "south," supplied from Jingsu's biography.

sentences.zh: 穀人五斛 各本並脫「人」字，據元龜二０七補。

translations.literal: Five hu per person—in all editions the character "person" is omitted; it is supplied according to Yuan Gui 207.
translations.idiomatic: "Five hu per person": all editions omit "person," supplied from Yuan Gui 207.

sentences.zh: 八月庚子 按是月癸亥朔，無庚子，初三日庚午，庚子或是庚午之譌。

translations.literal: On gengzi day in the eighth month—according to this month guihai was the first day of the month; there was no gengzi. The third day was gengwu; gengzi is probably a graphic error for gengwu.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day in the eighth month: that month began on guihai, so gengzi could not occur; the third day was gengwu—gengzi is probably a graphic error for gengwu.

sentences.zh: 而國度弘費「弘」各本並作「引」，據元龜四七一改。

translations.literal: Yet the state's revenues were lavishly spent—"lavishly" in all editions is written as "drawn forth"; it is changed according to Yuan Gui 471.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet the state's revenues were lavishly spent": all editions read "drawn forth" for "lavishly," corrected per Yuan Gui 471.

sentences.zh: 則氓隸齊歡「隸」各本並作「祇」，據元龜四七一改。

translations.literal: Then the common people rejoiced as one—"common people" in all editions is written as "only"; it is changed according to Yuan Gui 471.
translations.idiomatic: "Then the common people rejoiced as one": all editions read "only" for "common people," corrected per Yuan Gui 471.

sentences.zh: 驍騎將軍全景文為南豫州刺史「驍騎」各本並作「驃騎」，據南齊書呂安國傳全景文附傳改。

translations.literal: General of Agile Cavalry Quan Jingwen was made Inspector of South Yuzhou—"Agile Cavalry" in all editions is written as "Agile Cavalry General-in-Chief"; it is changed according to the biography of Quan Jingwen appended to the biography of Lü Anguo in the History of the Southern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: General of agile cavalry Quan Jingwen was made inspector of South Yuzhou: all editions read "general-in-chief of agile cavalry" for "general of agile cavalry," corrected per the biography of Quan Jingwen appended to Lü Anguo's biography in the History of the Southern Qi.
